tasks.task: Write a tenant notice, reminder or house rule letter

items.when: When a tenant must be told something in writing and the wording has to be calm and accurate
When the landlord's own draft is angry, to get a version the tenant will want to help with
When the letter is drafted, to cut legal-sounding padding so the tenant sees what to do and by when
When a notice hides the real message behind vague, official words

tasks.task: Chase late rent with fair, escalating messages

items.when: When rent is late and you need a friendly, a firmer and a final message that match the tenancy
Before you reply, to read the tenant's messages for hardship, anger or warning signs
When this tenant has a good record, to try a reminder that starts from the history and keeps goodwill
When the tenant cannot pay in full, to set a range they can meet and a firm follow-up
Before a hard call about arrears, to plan calm questions and test how a payment plan will hold
Before the final letter goes, to check the amount, the date and the next step are plain

tasks.task: Give notice of entry for a repair, inspection or viewing

items.when: When a contractor, inspector or viewer needs to get into an occupied home
When the visit also needs a repair update or a follow-up letter after a missed appointment
Before sending, to catch a wrong date, time or address and names spelt two ways

tasks.task: Sort repair reports by urgency and write work orders

items.when: When repair reports come in and each needs an urgency, a work order, access and a dated log line
When a tenant's repair message is long or upset, to pull out how urgent it really is
When the landlord has no written urgency rules, to set who does what and the edge cases
Each week, to find overdue decisions and jobs marked done with no proof of closure

tasks.task: Compare contractor quotes and keep the contractor list

items.when: When two or three contractors have quoted, to see cost, risk and terms side by side
When the owner wants one clear pick with the points to negotiate
Each month, to see which contractors to keep and whose terms or agreements need fixing
Before asking for quotes, to pull the repair history and what was paid last time

tasks.task: Write the monthly owner report

items.when: At month end, to tell an owner how the property did in five minutes of reading
When the report must be built from the rent ledger, bills and repair log
When the records are dated rows, to get monthly totals and rates you can trace back
When income fell or costs jumped, to rank the likely causes before you explain it to the owner
Before the report goes, to find broken formulas and totals that do not add up
When the report is drafted, to read it as the owner and list what they would have to ask

tasks.task: Run the monthly property routine across the portfolio

items.when: Each month and at the short weekly check, to work through rent, repairs, dates and reports in order
Each month, to see which tenancies, certificates and contracts fall due in the next 90 days
When an owner with many units wants the same numbers each week with a trend
When someone else covers the portfolio, to leave a note they can run from on day one

tasks.task: Reconcile rent received against the rent ledger

items.when: When you have the bank statement and the ledger, to get matches, near matches and what is left
When one payment will not match, to trace it to its source entries on both sides
When bills and repair costs need sorting by property and by type before the report
When the reconciled figures feed the owner's money in and money out lines

tasks.task: Write a fair rental advert and screening criteria

items.when: When a home is coming empty and needs an advert and written criteria applied the same to all
When the advert's first line is flat, to try five short headlines that each take a new angle
When the description is vague, to make each line true and easy to picture
Before the advert goes live, to catch wording or criteria that treat applicants unfairly
When you have two or three advert versions, to have a fresh reader pick one and say why

tasks.task: Answer rental enquiries and plan viewings

items.when: When enquiries arrive, to answer each with a draft reply and real viewing times
Before replying, to apply the same written criteria and questions to every applicant
When the home is still occupied and the sitting tenant must be told about viewings
Before the replies go, to catch a wrong rent, date or address

tasks.task: Run a tenancy from advert to deposit return

items.when: When a tenant gives notice or a new home is ready to let, to run every step in order
When you need the move-in pack: condition report, deposit papers and the documents to serve
When the tenancy agreement is new or unusual, to list risky or missing terms for a lawyer
When fixed terms and notice dates must not be missed across several homes

tasks.task: Write a tenant welcome guide and house manual

items.when: Before writing, to pull what the move-in pack already says about meters, keys and contacts
When you have rough notes on the home, to get a clean handout checked page by page
When tenants need the agreement's duties, payments and notice rules in plain words
When the guide is drafted, to cut it to what a new tenant will read and use

tasks.task: Propose deposit deductions at the end of a tenancy

items.when: When a tenancy has ended and the landlord wants to keep part of the deposit
When the tenant disputes a deduction, to build a dated timeline from emails and reports
When both sides are stuck, to find a third option and put the agreement in writing
Before sending, to check every deduction points to a dated photo, report or invoice

tasks.task: Reply to a tenant complaint or dispute

items.when: When a tenant writes in anger, to reply to the feeling, fix what you can and promise nothing false
When the complaint has a long history, to set out what happened and when before you answer
Before the reply goes, to test each promise in it against what the landlord can really do
When the reply must also serve as a formal repair update or house rule reminder
When the tenant and landlord are both dug in and a call must lower the heat

tasks.task: Check a landlord's compliance and keep the dates log

items.when: When a landlord with homes in England asks if they are compliant or takes on a new property
When safety certificates, checks and their expiry dates need one dated log
When certificates are missing or expired, to list each gap and draft the request to its owner
When your notes state a rule or deadline, to tie each to a dated official source or cut it

tasks.task: Plan and write a rent increase

items.when: When the increase needs the correct notice wording and period for the tenancy
When you want a covering letter that gives the reason and keeps a good tenant
Before setting the figure, to weigh the extra rent against the cost of an empty month
Before it is served, to check old rent, new rent and start date are impossible to misread

tasks.task: Run the numbers on a rental property deal

items.when: When a client brings a deal and needs buying costs, cash flow and yields worked out
When the deal needs a loan, to get monthly payments at quoted and higher rates
Before an offer, to set a value range, a walk-away price and the alternative to beat
When the numbers live in a spreadsheet, to find formula errors and broken links
When the asking price is treated as the value and nobody has asked about room for error

tasks.task: Stress test a deal for rates, empty months and repairs

items.when: Before an offer, to see cash flow when rates rise, the home sits empty or a big repair hits
When the landlord has other debts, to find the breaking point and size a cash cushion
When loans are on a floating rate, to work out the extra interest from a rate rise loan by loan
When the numbers look fine, to imagine the deal failed in a year and find the hidden bets
When a calm record hides one event that could force a sale
When the model is built, to have the figures recalculated and the key assumption named

tasks.task: Compare deals side by side and build a five-year hold view

items.when: When two or three deals must be compared on the same rules and the same costs
When you want returns shown across purchase price, debt, sale price and years held
When the client asks which deal to pick, to get payback and return with risks flagged
Before the comparison is shared, to check totals and state the key figures in plain words

tasks.task: List the questions to answer before an offer or a viewing

items.when: Before a viewing, to split the listing's claims from facts and plan what to check in person
When the client moves to an offer, to get documents, deadlines and choices from offer to closing
When the home comes with a sitting tenant or a lease, to list risky terms for a lawyer
When you need to know which unknowns change the numbers most, so those get asked first

tasks.task: Plan a year of repairs and upgrades within a budget

items.when: Before planning, to list repeat faults, ageing items and checks that fall due this year
When the owner has a fixed sum, to compare two plans that spend it in different ways
When you must show the owner the next 30, 60 and 90 days of rent in and bills out
When cover has not been reviewed, to list the risks and the questions to ask a broker

tasks.task: Get rental income and costs ready for the accountant

items.when: When a UK landlord files their own return, to list records, totals and accountant questions
When the year's receipts are a pile, to get them categorised with the gaps listed
When the owner is caught short each year, to set a rule for what to put aside from each rent
Before the file goes to the accountant, to check the ledger agrees with the bank

always.when: Before any letter or report goes out, to catch typos, wrong dates and names spelt two ways
When a document states a rule, a deadline or a figure, to tie it to a dated source or cut it

helpers.when: When the rent ledger and bank do not agree or the year's books need closing properly
When a block or large home needs a planned maintenance schedule and contractor management
When rules outside England apply or the owner needs a full evidence file for a regulator
When a home is let by the night and needs listings, guest messages and turnover plans
When a purchase or sale is under way and deadlines and documents must be tracked to closing
When the deal model or rent ledger needs building as a workbook the owner can reuse

gaps: No library item writes tenant notices, notices of entry or rent increase notices; only the kit covers them
No library item writes a rental listing advert or checks it against fair housing and discrimination rules
No library item sets tenant screening criteria or records how each applicant was scored
No library item builds a move-in inventory and condition report or compares it with the move-out state
No library item works out rental yield, cash flow after mortgage or a five-year hold for a property deal
No library item tracks landlord safety certificates such as gas, electrical and energy ratings by expiry date
No library item covers possession, eviction steps or tribunal papers for any country
No library item handles damp and mould reports, emergency call-outs or out-of-hours repair rules
No library item plans an arrears payment plan with a tenant or records one in writing
No library item covers property insurance claims or service charge budgets for blocks
No tool guide covers property management software such as rent ledgers and repair portals
